newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Police expect up to 100,000 at Brussels jobs march.
newsitem.headline: Police expect up to 100,000 at Brussels jobs march.

text.p: Police said on Thursday they expected up to 100,000 people to turn up for a march through Brussels on Sunday protesting at increasing job losses and insecurity.
The Brussels police department said in a statement they expected between 70,000 and 100,000 protesters, adding that 23 special trains and 500 coaches had already been booked.

Belgium has been shaken by the announcement in January of the closure of steelmaker Forges de Clabecq with the threatened loss of 1,800 jobs, and the more recent decision by French carmaker Renault to close its Belgian plant with the loss of 3,100 jobs.
There have been sporadic protests and marches in Brussels and elsewhere because of the Clabecq closure -- the most recent being on Wednesday.

But the employment issue took on international proportions and a diplomatic dimension when Renault suddenly announced at the end of February its decision to close the plant at Vilvoorde near Brussels.

Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene, who lives in Vilvoorde, condemned the decision and the lack of consultation, and the Belgian Federal and Flemish regional governments said they would take Renault to court.
French Prime Minister Alain Juppe carpeted Renault Chairman Louis Schweitzer, and even President Jacques Chirac was said to be angered at the manner in which the decision was made known.
Renault made matters worse by refusing to reverse its decision and declaring it would also shed more than 2,700 jobs in France this year.
Belgian Renault workers have taken their protest to France on several occasions -- including taking part in a demonstration on Tuesday in Paris with their colleagues from France and Spain.

Belgian union leaders have called for Sunday's march to be a major international event to force governments focused on budget cuts to get their economies ready for the European Union's single currency to realise the social consequences.
Workers from many of Belgium's neighbours -- but especially France -- are expected to take part in the march, and are several leading French and Belgian politicians.
